title: Multi-Dimensional Vector ISA Extension for Mobile In-Cache Computing
problem: Existing long-vector ISA extensions (RISC-V RVV, Arm SVE) provide only 1D strided and random memory accesses, which cannot efficiently utilize the 8192-lane SIMD width of in-SRAM vector engines built from mobile L2 caches because mobile data-parallel kernels expose limited 1D parallelism (average 635 elements) across multiple multi-dimensional data structures.
motivation: In-cache computing repurposes SRAM cache arrays into wide vector engines at low area cost, but without multi-dimensional memory access instructions the instruction issue bottleneck and low lane utilization (23% for bit-serial with RVV) prevent realizing their throughput advantage over conventional 128-bit mobile SIMD units.
method: MVE (Multi-dimensional Vector ISA Extension) enables processors to efficiently handle data arranged in up to 4 dimensions at once (like nested tables), rather than the 1D arrays that conventional processors are limited to. Execution control happens at the dimension level, using a compact mask register to activate or deactivate entire groups of iterations simultaneously, instead of controlling individual processing lanes. A specialized controller in the L2 cache converts multi-dimensional logical accesses into physical storage locations in the SRAM, using a transpose unit (with 8T bit-cells and a crossbar) to route data through all 8192 processing lanes (each 32 bits wide) in the right order, while managing L1 cache interactions to keep data consistent. The compiler supports this through data-lifetime analysis, hybrid instruction scheduling that mixes different strategies, and efficient register allocation to prevent unnecessary spills to main memory.
key_novelty: A vector instruction set that supports up to 4D memory accesses (with various stepping patterns and random access) and dimension-level masked execution (turning entire iteration groups on or off), hiding cache storage details from programmers while raising processing efficiency from 23% to 60% for mobile workloads.
contributions: MVE ISA with 4D strided and random memory accesses plus dimension-level masked execution, improving bit-serial in-cache utilization from 23% to 60% and performance by 3.8x over RISC-V RVV on the same engine
Cache architecture design with Transpose Memory Unit (TMU), crossbar, and MVE controller that abstracts cache geometry and maintains L1/L2 coherency
Compiler infrastructure (liveness analysis, list-hybrid scheduling, greedy register allocation) for in-cache register management
End-to-end evaluation on 44 kernels from 12 real mobile libraries showing 2.9x speedup and 8.8x energy reduction vs Arm Neon, and 9.3x speedup vs Adreno 640 GPU at 3.6% area overhead

metrics.speedup: 2.9x vs Arm Neon; 9.3x vs Adreno 640 GPU; 2.0x vs RISC-V RVV on same in-cache engine; 1.5x vs Duality Cache (SIMT model)
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 8.8x energy reduction vs Arm Neon; 5.2x energy reduction vs Adreno 640 GPU

baselines: RISC-V RVV on same in-cache bit-serial engine
limitations: MVE requires flushing dirty L2 cache lines to switch between cache and compute modes (taking under 2% of execution time in benchmarks), and performance degrades for workloads with large scalar instruction fractions (e.g., zlib reduction kernel achieves only 37% improvement).
primary_theme: multi-dimensional vector ISA for mobile in-SRAM computing
